text:
lee: quick thread: we've been chasing cold-start IO for large BLOOM-like models. idea: expose a tiny .ranges sidecar that lists byte-range descriptors + per-range MAC so clients can request only hot ranges and verify them cheaply while streaming. thoughts?

anya: how is this different from the index/manifest we've had?

lee: index lists tensors and offsets which is great for correctness but big to fetch. .ranges would be much smaller: e.g. 1 entry per 1MB window with a small MAC (HMAC-SHA256). clients can request the few first windows to warm prefixes and then fetch others on demand.

ravi: love the idea for prefix warmup. two concerns: 1) integrity model & signing; 2) on-disk mmap loaders that expect a canonical file layout.

jen: on (2) 100%. we cannot change safetensors raw layout. sidecar is non-invasive which is nice. but how do we handle range requests with some CDNs that don't support byte-range for compressed objects?

lee: suggestion: server can offer two hints: an HTTP header X-Weight-Ranges pointing to the sidecar URL, and X-Weight-Range-Granularity (e.g., 1MB). For compressed objects we fallback to sidecar + range fetch from uncompressed copy or a pre-flattened object store.

artifact-bot: note: artifact signer v2 now supports detached metadata signing (artifact.meta.sig). See docs: https://artifacts.internal/docs/signing

anya: integrity: per-range MACs are fine but we also need provenance. we should include a signed root (meta-hash + signature) so clients can trust sidecar without fetching the whole manifest.

ravi: operationally we also want to support delta-shards: store base + delta patches. sidecar could list whether range is base or delta and the patch op id. that lets us stream-apply small patches without full re-download.

lee: exactly. sidecar example below (minified):

```
{
  "version":"1",
  "granularity_bytes":1048576,
  "windows":[{"off":0,"len":1048576,"mac":"ab12...","type":"base"},{"off":1048576,"len":1048576,"mac":"cd34...","type":"delta","patch_id":"p-2026-03-20"}],
  "root_hash":"sha256:...",
  "root_sig":"sig-v2:..."
}
```

jen: nice. how does KV warmup API change? currently warmup accepts tensor ranges. we could add warmup_window(range_id, provisional=true) and mark entries provisional until verified by the root_sig. runtime needs to disallow provisional cache hits for production-safe routes.

anya: we should also add metrics: provisional_hit_rate, provisional_promote_latency, provisional_evictions. helps tune granularity.

ravi: CPU cost: recomputing MACs on client is cheap if windows are >256KB; but on many small windows it adds overhead. recommend conservative default of 1MB-4MB and expose server hint for "fast-verify" mode that uses no MACs but requires full-manifest fetch for final verification.

lee: good. another perf trick: allow server to return a small bloom-filter of hot windows so clients can prioritize which windows to request first (e.g., attention-heavy weights). bloom is tiny and probabilistic.

jen: edge case: rollback if patch mismatch during streaming-apply. we must provide an atomic patch-apply API on the runtime to avoid inconsistent KV state. rollbacks should unpin provisional windows and optionally re-request trusted variant.

artifact-bot: reminder: new canary deployment for range-sidecar will run in eng-ml/warmup-experiments at 23:00 UTC.

anya: next steps I propose: 1) draft a short RFC describing .ranges sidecar format + signing; 2) add warmup_window provisional flag + tombstone semantics; 3) implement server headers and optional bloom-hint; 4) run canary and collect provisional metrics. I'll stub the RFC today.

lee: I'll add a tiny test harness: curl range + meta fetch. example command: 

```
# fetch first two windows and verify locally
curl -H "Range: bytes=0-2097151" -sS https://objstore/models/mymodel/shard-000.safetensors -o shard.part
curl -sS https://objstore/models/mymodel/shard-000.ranges -o shard.ranges.json
# verify macs locally: (pseudo)
python3 tools/verify_windows.py --ranges shard.ranges.json --file shard.part
```

ravi: cool. +1. please include a couple regression tests for mmap loader paths (ensure offsets unchanged) and CDN behavior.

jen: and add a small design note about compatibility with existing manifestless warmup experiments. we don't want to fragment the ecosystem.

lee: will do. thanks all :rocket:
